Isolated application evidence in scripts/probes/hunts/legacy-seam-evidence.mjs. Duplicate campaign membership and scan replay preserve one progression credit. A post-capture interruption leaves the engagement and capture rows without replaying the downstream award. Competing requests at exhausted capacity preserve the existing capture and issue zero credits. An existing reward grant prevents a second Zap entry. Fresh Hunt evidence replays independently of an existing same-day Regulars stamp. The fixture runs the shipped orchestrators against in-memory database and side-effect boundaries. D1's adapter remains the transactional Hunt claim RPC with independent placement evidence and a durable outbox. The original scarcity-race acceptance remains open. Evidence is isolated from live scans, provider activity, and production database behavior.

Closed 2026-11-16: scripts/probes/hunts/legacy-seams.mjs is the single entry for all five seams and exits non-zero on a wrong surviving record. The last-unit scarcity race is now reproduced: on the legacy path two members competing for the last unit of a capped code both pass (two captures, two ledger rows, two Zap awards against a cap of one), because lib/engagement/verify.ts counts and lib/engagement/capture.ts inserts with no lock between them. The adapter boundary for scarcity is public.hunt_reward_grant (reward row lock plus the stock check constraint); the shipped caller turns its answers into one grant and one sold_out with terms. Proven in the fixture only: no Postgres race was run. supabase/tests/hunt_rewards.test.sql proves the sequential last unit. The legacy oversell and the unrun two-session proof are FH-002S.
